story: On Monday evening in Sumter Oaks, the humid October air hangs hazy and warm at 75 degrees as the town settles in. Gary, content after a few lucky rounds of pickleball, is still at the Rec Center, where Donna, triumphant and already penciling him in as her doubles partner on the ladder board for Saturday, is cheerfully refusing to let him leave. Over at Town Square, Hal is dutifully checking the parade sign-up sheet to see whether Gary's cart made the cut, while Rosa, determined to keep the neighborhood fed and friendly, pins a handwritten dinner invitation to the Magnolia Loop bulletin board.
events: Hal (parade signup table): Read the sign-up sheet to see whether Gary's cart is entered in the parade
Rosa (street bulletin board): Pin up a handwritten welcome dinner invitation for Gary, Donna, and Hal at my place, with food and no cart or flamingo debates

gary.thought_process: Donna handed me the paddle and we've been rallying at court 1 for a while. It's 7:17 PM, nearly dinner time at Rosa's at six, which I passed along to Donna earlier, so no need to repeat it. I've never played before and I'm a bit out of my element, but it feels good to be included. I should keep my attention on the game and give her honest feedback on how I'm doing, then wrap up soon and get back to the garage to work on the cart lights and speaker for the parade. The loud sound system will need to respect L-03 quiet hours, and the lights and mods need Architectural Review under L-01. For now, I keep the rally going and chat a little.

parameters.content: Well, I got three in a row over the net, so I'm calling myself a natural. Another few and I'll head home to my garage, though. That cart won't wire itself for the parade.

donna.thought_process: Gary has been on court 1 with the spare paddle for a while now, and it's already past seven in the evening. Rosa's dinner is at six, so he's likely late for it, and I don't want to be the reason he skips it. I've got him hooked on the basics, so now it's time to lock in the partnership while he's feeling good. I won't repeat the invitation. I should praise his progress, then get him committed to Saturday morning and the ladder, and send him off to dinner. Partners keep moving to Ocala, so I need a firm yes.

parameters.content: Gary, look at you, you're a natural! Go on to Rosa's before she sends out a search party, but I'm putting us down as doubles partners on the ladder board, Saturday at eight. Don't you dare say no.

hal.thought_process: Both complaints are filed and logged, and I've double-checked the dates and violation codes. I'm back in the Town Square with nobody around at 7:17 PM and nothing more to do on that front. Gary at least owned up to the wiring, which I'll give him, and I did find myself thinking the street was quieter before that speaker. The parade signup table is right here. If Gary's cart is headed for the parade, the sign-up sheet will show whether he plans to roll it out before the review committee has seen a single wire. A supply sergeant likes to check the paperwork, so I'll look it over.

parameters.content: Read the sign-up sheet to see whether Gary's cart is entered in the parade

rosa.thought_process: I'm back on Magnolia Loop at 7:17 PM and nobody is in sight. I invited Hal this morning, but Gary and Donna haven't gotten a word from me, and I still don't know where I stand with the three of them. The street bulletin board is the obvious place to post a welcome dinner invitation that reaches all of them at once, no chasing required. I'll put up a short, friendly notice, which also fits my blunt, practical streak.

parameters.content: Pin up a handwritten welcome dinner invitation for Gary, Donna, and Hal at my place, with food and no cart or flamingo debates

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
